module_title: Mauryan Empire - Ashoka’s Edicts, Dhamma Policy, and Causes of Decline
introduction: At an advanced level, the study of Ashoka’s edicts, his Dhamma policy, and the causes of the Mauryan Empire’s decline becomes crucial. These topics are not only factual but also analytical in nature and are frequently asked in exams. At this level, we will examine the features of edicts, policies, and reasons for decline in depth.

core_concepts.title: Types of Ashoka’s Edicts
core_concepts.description: Ashoka’s edicts are mainly classified into Rock Edicts, Pillar Edicts, and Minor Rock Edicts. These inscriptions contain messages related to Dhamma, administration, and moral conduct.

core_concepts.title: Dhamma Policy
core_concepts.description: Ashoka’s Dhamma policy was based on moral living, non-violence, religious tolerance, and welfare of the people. It was not the promotion of a single religion but a guide for ethical conduct in society.

core_concepts.title: Significance of Major Edicts
core_concepts.description: The 13th Rock Edict describes the Kalinga War and Ashoka’s remorse, while other edicts provide moral instructions and guidelines for the people.

core_concepts.title: Language and Script
core_concepts.description: Ashoka’s edicts were written in Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts. Most were in Prakrit language, while some were also found in Greek and Aramaic.

core_concepts.title: Decline of the Mauryan Empire
core_concepts.description: After Ashoka, weak successors, difficulty in controlling a vast empire, administrative inefficiency, and economic issues became the major causes of the decline of the Mauryan Empire.

important_entities.name: 13th Rock Edict
important_entities.significance: Evidence of Ashoka’s transformation and Dhamma policy

important_entities.name: Brahmi Script
important_entities.significance: Considered the mother of Indian scripts

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Most inscriptions mention 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' instead of 'Ashoka'. The name 'Ashoka' appears only in a few inscriptions like Maski and Gujarra.
It is incorrect to equate Dhamma strictly with Buddhism. It was a broader ethical policy applicable to all religions.
Brahmi is written from left to right, whereas Kharosthi is written from right to left. Reversing this is a common mistake.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps remember the three main types of Ashoka’s edicts.
Helps recall the direction of writing for both scripts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Weak rulers, vast empire, weak administration
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Summarizes the key causes of the Mauryan decline.

exam_strategy_tips: If the question mentions the '13th Rock Edict', link it to the Kalinga War and Ashoka’s remorse.
In questions related to Dhamma, understand it as an ethical policy rather than a strictly religious doctrine.
